# Beads Workflow Context

> **Context Recovery**: Run `bd prime` after compaction, clear, or new session
> Hooks auto-call this in Claude Code when a beads workspace is resolved

# 🚨 SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL 🚨

**CRITICAL**: Before saying "done" or "complete", you MUST run this checklist:

```
[ ] 1. git status              (check what changed)
[ ] 2. git add <files>         (stage code changes)
[ ] 3. git commit -m "..."     (commit code)
[ ] 4. git push                (push to remote)
```

**NEVER skip this.** Work is not done until pushed.

## Core Rules
- **Default**: Use beads for ALL task tracking (`bd create`, `bd ready`, `bd close`)
- **Prohibited**: Do NOT use TodoWrite, TaskCreate, or markdown files for task tracking
- **Workflow**: Create beads issue BEFORE writing code, mark in_progress when starting
- **Memory**: Use `bd remember "insight"` for persistent knowledge across sessions. Do NOT use MEMORY.md files — they fragment across accounts. Search with `bd memories <keyword>`.
- Persistence you don't need beats lost context
- Git workflow: beads auto-commit to Dolt, run `git push` at session end
- Session management: check `bd ready` for available work

## Essential Commands

### Finding Work
- `bd ready` - Show issues ready to work (no blockers)
- `bd list --status=open` - All open issues
- `bd list --status=in_progress` - Your active work
- `bd show <id>` - Detailed issue view with dependencies

### Creating & Updating
- `bd create --title="Summary of this issue" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task|bug|feature --priority=2` - New issue
  - Priority: 0-4 or P0-P4 (0=critical, 2=medium, 4=backlog). NOT "high"/"medium"/"low"
- `bd update <id> --claim` - Claim work
- `bd update <id> --assignee=username` - Assign to someone
- `bd update <id> --title/--description/--notes/--design` - Update fields inline
- `bd close <id>` - Mark complete
- `bd close <id1> <id2> ...` - Close multiple issues at once (more efficient)
- `bd close <id> --reason="explanation"` - Close with reason
- **Tip**: When creating multiple issues/tasks/epics, use parallel subagents for efficiency
- **WARNING**: Do NOT use `bd edit` - it opens $EDITOR (vim/nano) which blocks agents

### Dependencies & Blocking
- `bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>` - Add dependency (issue depends on depends-on)
- `bd blocked` - Show all blocked issues
- `bd show <id>` - See what's blocking/blocked by this issue

### Sync & Collaboration
- `bd dolt push` - Push beads to Dolt remote
- `bd dolt pull` - Pull beads from Dolt remote
- `bd search <query>` - Search issues by keyword

### Project Health
- `bd stats` - Project statistics (open/closed/blocked counts)
- `bd doctor` - Check for issues (sync problems, missing hooks)
- `bd doctor --check=conventions` - Check for convention drift (lint, stale, orphans)

### Quality Tools
- `bd create --validate` - Check description has required sections
- `bd create --acceptance="criteria"` - Set acceptance criteria (checked by --validate)
- `bd create --design="decisions"` - Record design decisions
- `bd create --notes="context"` - Add supplementary notes
- `bd config set validation.on-create warn` - Auto-validate on every create
- `bd lint` - Check existing issues for missing sections

### Lifecycle & Hygiene
- `bd defer <id> --until="date"` - Defer work to a future date
- `bd supersede <id> --with=<new-id>` - Mark issue as superseded
- `bd close <id> --suggest-next` - Show newly unblocked issues after closing
- `bd stale` - Find issues with no recent activity
- `bd orphans` - Find issues with broken dependencies
- `bd preflight` - Pre-PR checks (lint, stale, orphans)
- `bd human <id>` - Flag for human decision (list/respond/dismiss)

### Structured Workflows
- `bd formula list` - See available workflow templates
- `bd mol pour <name>` - Start structured workflow from formula

## Common Workflows

**Starting work:**
```bash
bd ready           # Find available work
bd show <id>       # Review issue details
bd update <id> --claim  # Claim it
```

**Completing work:**
```bash
bd close <id1> <id2> ...    # Close all completed issues at once
git add . && git commit -m "..."  # Commit code changes
git push                    # Push to remote
```

**Creating dependent work:**
```bash
# Run bd create commands in parallel (use subagents for many items)
bd create --title="Implement feature X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=feature
bd create --title="Write tests for X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task
bd dep add beads-yyy beads-xxx  # Tests depend on Feature (Feature blocks tests)
```

○ rcballot-8yx · Add unit test suite for voting algorithms (processRCV.js, processCondorcet.js)   [● P1 · OPEN]
Owner: Stuart Donaldson · Type: task
Created: 2026-07-14 · Updated: 2026-07-14

DESCRIPTION
npm test currently runs test_gas_logger, test_ballot_model, test_manage_deployments, test_callwebapp — zero coverage of the five voting algorithms. That is how the blank-rank bug (RankChoiceVoting-35e) shipped.

Create test/test_voting_algorithms.js following the existing test style (plain node asserts, loaded via eval or module pattern like the other tests; processRCV.js/processCondorcet.js are bare GAS-style globals — load with fs.readFileSync + eval and stub global.Logger, as no module.exports exists; alternatively add a module.exports guard like webAdmin.js line 484 has, which is the cleaner route). Wire it into the package.json test script.

Boundary conditions to cover for RCV (runRankedChoiceVoting):
- majority winner in round 1
- winner after elimination cascade (verify redistribution)
- exhausted ballots: majority threshold must use active-ballot weights, not all ballots
- weighted ballots in first-choice counting AND in tie-breaks (RankChoiceVoting-c6n)
- partial ballots / blank ranks, incl. a candidate ranked by nobody (RankChoiceVoting-35e)
- non-contiguous ranks compressed correctly (e.g. 1,3,7 -> 1,2,3)
- tie broken by fewest second-choice; tie broken by most last-place; unresolvable tie returns {winner:null, tie:[...]}
- 2-candidate dead 50/50 tie
- single ballot; all-blank ballot; duplicate rank values on one ballot
- summary table statuses consistent with returned winner

For Condorcet family (buildPairwiseMatrix, findCondorcetWinner, findSchulzeWinner, findRankedPairsWinner, findMinimaxWinner):
- pairwise matrix correctness incl. weights and partial ballots (ranked beats unranked)
- clear Condorcet winner found by all four methods
- perfect 3-cycle: basic=null, minimax/schulze/rankedPairs behavior per their specs (rankedPairs per RankChoiceVoting-vi6)
- pairwise exact tie between two candidates
- 2 candidates only; known textbook example where Schulze winner differs from plurality
- minimax tied worst-defeat returns winner:null

Write tests to assert CORRECT behavior; tests for the three open bugs will fail until those are fixed — that is intended (fix beads are dependencies).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
test/test_voting_algorithms.js exists, wired into npm test, all listed boundary conditions asserted, npm test passes once dependency bugs are fixed.

DEPENDS ON
  → ✓ rcballot-35e: Blank ranks treated as best rank: an unranked candidate can win every algorithm ● P1
  → ✓ rcballot-c6n: RCV tie-break ignores ballot weights (counts ballots, not votes) ● P2
  → ✓ rcballot-vi6: Ranked Pairs silently picks an order-dependent winner on cycles and pairwise ties ● P2

+// Minimal stand-in for a Sheet: just enough for logProcess()'s appendRow() calls
+// so tests can inspect which round/candidate/explanation got logged.
+  // Round 1: A=2, B=3, C=4, total=9, majority>4.5 -> no winner, A (fewest) eliminated.
+  // Round 2: A's 2 ballots redistribute to B -> B=5, C=4, total=9 -> B wins.
+  // Round 1: A=2 (exhausted-only ballots), B=3, C=4, total=9, majority 4.5 -> no winner.
+  // A eliminated (fewest). A's ballots have no other rank -> exhausted in round 2.
+  // Round 2: B=3, C=4; if majority correctly uses ACTIVE ballots (7, not 9),
+  // threshold is 3.5 and C=4 wins immediately in round 2.
+  assert.ok(winsInRound2, 'expected C to be declared winner in round 2 using active-ballot majority');
+  // First-choice counting must use ballot weight, not ballot count: A=5, B=1, total=6.
+// Repro-style coverage: raw ranks with gaps (1,3,7) must compress to (1,2,3)
+// and drive redistribution identically to already-contiguous ranks.
+  // Same shape as testEliminationCascadeRedistribution but B's rank is raw "9"
+  // instead of "2" - compression must still treat it as B's second choice.
+    [1, 1, 2], // A and B both marked rank 1 on the same ballot
+  // Must not throw; stable sort keeps the first-listed duplicate (A) as the
+// RCV: tie-break ladder (fewest second-choice -> most last-place -> unresolved)
+    // Re-derive concretely below instead of via this placeholder map; see explicit ballots.
+  // Explicit, unambiguous ballots (first-choice counts: A=1, B=1, C=2, D=2):
+    { voterName: 'v1', ranks: [1, 2, 3, 4], weight: 1 }, // A first, B second
+    { voterName: 'v2', ranks: [2, 1, 3, 4], weight: 1 }, // B first, A second
+    { voterName: 'v3', ranks: [2, 1, 3, 4], weight: 1 }, // C first, A second
+    { voterName: 'v4', ranks: [2, 1, 3, 4], weight: 1 }, // C first, A second
+    { voterName: 'v5', ranks: [2, 1, 4, 3], weight: 1 }, // D first, A second
+    { voterName: 'v6', ranks: [2, 1, 4, 3], weight: 1 }, // D first, A second
+  // Candidate order here is [A,B,C,D]; but "C first"/"D first" ballots above are
+  // impossible to express with rank 2 both meaning "B" - build with explicit
+    { A: 1, B: 2, C: 3, D: 4 }, // A first, B second
+    { A: 2, B: 1, C: 3, D: 4 }, // B first, A second
+    { A: 2, B: 3, C: 1, D: 4 }, // C first, A second
+    { A: 2, B: 3, C: 1, D: 4 }, // C first, A second
+    { A: 2, B: 3, C: 4, D: 1 }, // D first, A second
+    { A: 2, B: 3, C: 4, D: 1 }, // D first, A second
+  // First-choice: A=1, B=1, C=2, D=2 -> tie for fewest is A,B.
+  // Second-choice tally among A,B across all ballots: A=5 (v2..v6), B=1 (v1).
+  // B has fewest second-choice votes -> B is eliminated.
+    { A: 1, B: 2, C: 3, D: 4 }, // A first; B second; D last
+    { B: 1, A: 2, C: 3, D: 4 }, // B first; A second; D last
+    { C: 1, D: 2, A: 3, B: 4 }, // C first; B last
+    { C: 1, D: 2, A: 3, B: 4 }, // C first; B last
+    { D: 1, C: 2, A: 3, B: 4 }, // D first; B last
+    { D: 1, C: 2, A: 3, B: 4 }, // D first; B last
+  // First-choice: A=1, B=1, C=2, D=2 -> tie for fewest is A,B.
+  // Second-choice tally among A,B: row1->B, row2->A, rows3/4->D(skip), rows5/6->C(skip)
+  // Last-place tally among A,B: row1/2 last=D(skip); rows3-6 last=B (4 times); A never last
+  //   => A=0, B=4 -> B has the MOST last-place votes -> B eliminated.
+    { A: 1, B: 2, C: 3, D: 4 }, // A first, B second, D last
+    { B: 1, A: 2, C: 3, D: 4 }, // B first, A second, D last
+    { C: 1, A: 2, B: 3, D: 4 }, // C first, A second, D last
+    { C: 1, B: 2, A: 3, D: 4 }, // C first, B second, D last
+    { D: 1, A: 2, B: 3, C: 4 }, // D first, A second, C last
+    { D: 1, B: 2, A: 3, C: 4 }, // D first, B second, C last
+  // First-choice: A=1, B=1, C=2, D=2 -> tie for fewest is A,B.
+  // Second-choice among A,B: row1->B, row2->A, row3->A, row4->B, row5->A, row6->B => A=3,B=3 (tied).
+  // Last-place among A,B: never A or B (always C or D) => A=0,B=0 (tied).
+  // Neither tie-breaker resolves it -> manual review, winner:null.
// Repro from rcballot-35e: 3 ballots unanimously rank A over B, nobody ranks C.
// A blank rank cell must not be treated as better than an actual rank.
+// Partial ballots: a voter who only ranks some candidates shouldn't have blanks

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/stuar/.claude/skills/work-log

# /work-log

Keep a project activity log without manual formatting. Date headers, consistent structure, single atomic append. As of v3 the entry is **segmented**: a session is captured as an ordered set of objective segments, each carrying the matured rationale (the *why*), the outcome, and a facing tag, so the log doubles as the capture substrate that downstream blog and changelog renders read from.

## When to Use

**Explicit (no filter):** `/work-log` alone at end of session to auto-summarize what was accomplished.

**Explicit (with filter):** `/work-log "focus area"` to extract only session work matching that prompt (e.g., `/work-log "tests"` logs only test-related work).

**Auto-trigger:** Could extend to fire on session end or after `git commit`.

**Gate:** End of work session; post-commit or before pushing.

**Not needed:** Trivial sessions with no decision or outcome worth recording.

## Addresses

- Manual work log entry forgotten or lost
- Inconsistent formatting (missing date headers, wrong indentation)
- Multiple file writes instead of atomic append
- Rationale (the *why* and rejected alternatives) lost when only the mechanical *what* is logged
- Objective drift/accretion within a session flattened into a single false through-line

## Input

**Type:** Command invocation
**Format:** `/work-log` (auto-summarize) or `/work-log [filter prompt]` (guided capture)
**Required:** Nothing (defaults to auto-summary)
**Optional:** Filter prompt to identify specific session work (e.g., "bug fixes", "tests", "documentation")
**Minimum:** `/work-log`

## Entry format

An entry is one or more `### Objective N:` blocks under a single timestamp header. Immediately under the header, emit a terse provenance line naming the session transcript and the schema version this entry was written under: `_session <id> · v3 · <span>_` (e.g. `_session 29d5bd53 · v3 · 06-20→06-22_`). Record the **bare session id**, not the full transcript path, so an audit can locate the file by globbing `~/.claude/projects/*/<id>.jsonl` even if the project later moves. The `v3` token is the schema version (this format); it lets an audit validate each entry against the rules it was written under, so older entries never need retroactive revision when the format evolves. Each block:

- **Objective N: `<label>`** — a distinct goal the work pursued. Append `[accreted]` when this objective was picked up *after* the session had already started on a different one.
- **Transition:** (accreted objectives only) why this objective was picked up mid-session, e.g. warm context made it cheaper to do now than to reconstruct cold later, or a correction/redirect forced it.
- **Rationale:** the matured *why*, as understood at the end of the segment, not the provisional framing it opened with. Quote the developer's own words verbatim where they carry the rationale or a correction.
- **Rejected:** (only if applicable) an approach tried and discarded, or a design the developer explicitly overrode, and why.
- **Outcome [`<facing>`]:** what actually resulted. Tag each outcome with its audience: `user-facing`, `developer-facing`, or `internal`. Emit more than one Outcome line if a segment produced changes at different facings.
- **Open:** (only if applicable) a question or thread left unresolved at session end.

Optionally close the whole entry with `### Key Learnings:` for non-obvious platform/environment discoveries (orthogonal to rationale: these are facts about the world, not decisions).

**Facing tag definitions** (drive the differentiated changelog render):
- `user-facing` — visible to whoever operates/uses the tool (new command, changed flag, behavior an operator would notice).
- `developer-facing` — visible to someone working on the code (new module, refactor, test infrastructure, API/contract change).
- `internal` — neither; incidental cleanup, notes, exploration with no shipped change.

**Granularity rule (important):** open a new `### Objective` only when the *work* turns to a genuinely distinct goal. Fold incidental fixes, one-off questions, and momentary digressions into the segment that surfaced them (a single clarifying Q&A or a small bug hit while doing other work is not its own objective). Prefer four honest segments over nine over-cut ones. A focused single-goal session is exactly one Objective block.

## Confirmation gate

Fire the gate **only when uncertain**, so it never becomes rubber-stamp theater:

- **Trigger:** you *inferred* an objective or rationale rather than the developer stating it, OR the arc turned into two or more segments. A session that opened with one clearly stated goal and stayed on it needs no confirmation; write it and skip the gate.
- **Ask:** present the proposed segmentation as a concrete default the developer can accept in one keystroke ("here's how I'd split this session and why, confirm or re-cut"). Target the *specific* uncertain spots, not the whole entry: an outcome inferred from the absence of a resolution message, a causal link inferred from proximity, and the segment boundaries themselves. Allow "mixed / no single objective" as a valid answer, and never manufacture a through-line that was not there.
- **Degrade gracefully:** if the developer does not answer, record the entry with the inferred fields marked (e.g. `Rationale (inferred):`), do not block.

## Procedure

1. **Determine mode** → If an argument is provided, use it as a filter prompt (guided capture); otherwise auto-summarize.
2. **Segment the session** → Split the session into objective segments per the granularity rule. Mark accreted objectives and their transition reason. For each segment derive the matured rationale (quoting the developer where their words carry it), any rejected alternative, the outcome(s) with a facing tag each, and any open thread.
3. **Run the confirmation gate** → If its trigger conditions hold, confirm the inferred spots with the developer before writing; otherwise proceed.
4. **Include header + provenance** → Write `## YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (current date/time), then a `_session <id> · v3 · <span>_` line. The `v3` literal is the schema version this format writes; keep it verbatim. Capture the id mechanically: the active session is the most-recently-modified `*.jsonl` under `~/.claude/projects/` in the encoded dir for the current project (the cwd with `/` replaced by `-`), e.g. `ls -t ~/.claude/projects/$(pwd | sed 's#/#-#g')/*.jsonl 2>/dev/null | head -1`, then take the basename minus `.jsonl` as `<id>`. This is mechanical metadata, orthogonal to the segmentation judgment. If the id cannot be resolved, write `_session unknown · v3_` rather than blocking.
5. **Append via heredoc** → Run `cat >> work-log.md << 'EOF'` with the header and the segmented entry in a single Bash call | Fail: display error, abort, suggest manual edit.
6. **Display result** → Show the appended entry (tail the file) | Fail: read-back failed; user should verify manually.
7. **Nudge a periodic audit** → After displaying the entry, show a brief notice that the log should be reviewed periodically (not every session): `Periodically audit this log: python3 ~/.claude/skills/work-log-audit/scripts/work-log-lint.py work-log.md --since <adoption-date> --coverage`. This is how coverage gets checked across the many projects worked in a day.
8. **Suggest context clear** → Display message: "Cache context grown large? Run `/clear` to clean up session history." | Do not auto-invoke /clear.

## Success Criteria
- Entry is segmented: one or more `### Objective` blocks, each with Rationale and at least one facing-tagged Outcome
- Accreted objectives carry a `Transition:` line; single-goal sessions are exactly one block
- Every Outcome carries a facing tag (`user-facing` / `developer-facing` / `internal`)
- Entry carries a `_session <id> · v3_` provenance line with the bare session id and the schema version (verify: line present under the header; the id resolves via `~/.claude/projects/*/<id>.jsonl` or is explicitly `unknown`; the `v3` token is present)
- Confirmation gate fired when (and only when) an objective/rationale was inferred or the arc turned
- Rationale reflects the matured why and quotes the developer verbatim where their words carry it
- Entry appended to work-log.md (verify: `tail` shows new content with no truncation)
- Date and time header exists and matches now (verify: `grep "## YYYY-MM-DD"` returns current date and time `HH:MM:SS`)
- File remains readable and valid (verify: file size increased, bash command returned 0)
- Cache-clear suggestion displayed (verify: message shown, no auto `/clear` invoked)

## Examples

### Example 1: Focused single-objective session (no gate)

**Input:** `/work-log`

**Expected output:**
```
## 2026-05-08 20:33:01
_session a1b2c3d4 · v3 · 05-08_

### Objective 1: Fix auth validation bug in the login flow
Rationale: Login accepted malformed tokens; "we want the validator to reject before the session is minted, not after."
Outcome [user-facing]: Malformed tokens now rejected at login with a clear error.
Outcome [developer-facing]: Added 12 unit tests covering the validation paths.

### Key Learnings:
`clasp run function` requires a GCP project plus a custom OAuth screen.
```

### Example 2: Multi-objective session with accretion (gate fires)

**Input:** `/work-log`

**Expected output:**
```
## 2026-06-21 14:39:47
_session 29d5bd53 · v3 · 06-20→06-21_

### Objective 1: Get a first successful slackdump run against a real workspace
Rationale: Prove the local-first path end to end before automating anything.
Outcome [user-facing]: First token/cookie capture and slackdump run succeeded against f3pugetsound.

### Objective 2: Build a workspace-registration tool  [accreted]
Transition: picked up immediately once manual capture worked, to avoid repeating the console dance per workspace while that context was warm.
Rationale: A tool run with the cookie as an argument that finishes registration from the harvested snippet.
Rejected: the first auto-import design was overridden. "you botched this. I want to run a command 'register-workspace' workspace-url-or-name xoxd-cookie."
Outcome [user-facing]: register-workspace built to the specified CLI contract; no-arg invocation lists known workspaces and registration status.
Open: duplicate f3kirkland entry flagged for deletion, not confirmed before session end.
```
(Here the gate would confirm the two-segment split, the "warm context" transition reason, and that the duplicate-entry thread was genuinely left open.)

## Anti-Pattern

**Pattern:** Overwriting file with `>` instead of appending with `>>`
**Symptom:** Entire work log history lost, file contains only most recent entry
**Prevented by:** Procedure always uses `>>` (append) and single-call heredoc
**Found:** Bash errors when testing initial implementation

**Pattern:** Over-segmenting — a new `### Objective` for every topic shift or clarifying question
**Symptom:** A single session produces eight or nine thin segments; the log becomes noise
**Prevented by:** The granularity rule — fold incidental work into the segment that surfaced it

## Related

- **git commit messages** — source of truth for individual changes; work-log summarizes sessions
- **blog-generate** — narrative render over the accumulated segmented log (rationale included); reads this substrate, does not re-derive from transcripts
- **changelog-generate** — differentiated CHANGELOG filtered by the facing tag (user-facing vs developer-facing); a re-phrasing pass over Outcomes, anchored to a version/date cut
- **extract_context.py digest** — backfill/audit tool that mines transcripts for rationale when a session was never logged
- **capture audit** — uses each entry's `_session` id to pair the entry with its transcript (fidelity check) and to enumerate sessions that have no entry (coverage check)
